filament.name: Proto-pasta High Temp Carbon Fiber PLA

heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P requires upgrading to a hardened steel nozzle and extruder gear before running abrasive Proto-pasta High Temp Carbon Fiber PLA safely. With the upgrade installed, it reliably prints at speeds up to 155 mm/s constrained by a safe 13 mm³/s volumetric flow limit.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with clean surface (optional PVP glue stick as release aid)
slicerTweaks: Cap the Max Volumetric Speed at 13 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at high print speeds.
Increase default nozzle temperature to 220°C (first layer 225°C) to compensate for the lower thermal conductivity of hardened steel.
Set outer wall speed to 100 mm/s and inner walls/infill to 155 mm/s to optimize matte surface finish and dimensional stability.
Set Retraction Distance to 0.8 mm and uncheck 'Wipe while retracting' or keep wipe distance to 1 mm to reduce micro-clog risk from milled carbon fibers.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking and severe under-extrusion mid-print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Aggressive volumetric flow exceeding 13 mm³/s or fiber agglomeration in a 0.4 mm nozzle tip.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lower maximum volumetric flow to 12-13 mm³/s and increase printing temperature by 5°C to drop melt viscosity.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rapid bore wear and inconsistent extrusion line width
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Using the stock P1P stainless steel nozzle, which erodes quickly from abrasive milled carbon fibers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install Bambu Lab original Hardened Steel Complete Hotend Assembly and Hardened Extruder Gear.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough, brittle perimeter walls and poor layer adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption by the PLA base polymer degrading melt strength during extrusion.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated filament dryer at 50°C for 6 hours before printing.

faq.question: Can I print Proto-pasta CF-PLA with the stock P1P stainless steel hotend?
faq.answer: No, the carbon fiber particles will wear down the stock stainless steel nozzle in under 250 grams of printing, causing rapid bore enlargement and extrusion failure.

faq.question: Does Proto-pasta High Temp Carbon Fiber PLA need an enclosure on the P1P?
faq.answer: No, it is a PLA-based composite that benefits from open-frame airflow; printing in an open chamber prevents heat creep and preserves sharp details.

faq.question: What is the post-print annealing process for this material?
faq.answer: To achieve high-temperature resistance, bake the finished print in an oven at 95°C to 110°C for 30 to 60 minutes, accounting for slight dimensional shrinkage.

faq.question: Is it safe to run this filament through the Bambu Lab AMS?
faq.answer: Proto-pasta CF-PLA is somewhat brittle and abrasive; it can be used in the AMS, but prolonged use will wear down standard plastic funnels and PTFE tubes unless wear-resistant guides are installed.
